number_of_islands.optimal:
sink(grid, r, c):   (turn the whole island containing (r, c) into water)
    grid[r][c] = '0', stack = [(r, c)]
    while the stack is not empty:
        (x, y) = pop the top
        for each in-bounds neighbour (nx, ny) with grid[nx][ny] == '1':
            grid[nx][ny] = '0'   (mark on push, not on pop, so no cell is pushed twice)
            push (nx, ny)
count = 0
for each cell (r, c) with grid[r][c] == '1':
    count += 1
    sink(grid, r, c)
return count

rotting_oranges.brute:
minutes = 0
repeat:
    next_grid = copy of grid, changed = false   (rot into a copy so the minute happens at once)
    for each cell (r, c) with grid[r][c] == 2:
        for each in-bounds neighbour (nr, nc) with grid[nr][nc] == 1:
            next_grid[nr][nc] = 2, changed = true
    if not changed: stop
    grid = next_grid, minutes += 1
if any 1 is left in grid: return -1
return minutes
rotting_oranges.optimal:
queue = empty deque, fresh = 0
for each cell (r, c):
    if grid[r][c] == 2: push (r, c) to the back
    else if grid[r][c] == 1: fresh += 1
minutes = 0
while the queue is not empty and fresh > 0:
    for each cell currently in the queue:   (exactly the oranges that rotted last minute)
        (r, c) = pop from the front
        for each in-bounds neighbour (nr, nc) with grid[nr][nc] == 1:
            grid[nr][nc] = 2, fresh -= 1
            push (nr, nc) to the back
    minutes += 1
if fresh > 0: return -1
return minutes

pacific_atlantic_water_flow.brute:
result = []
for each cell (start_r, start_c):
    seen = {start}, stack = [start], pacific = false, atlantic = false
    while the stack is not empty:
        (r, c) = pop the top
        if r == 0 or c == 0: pacific = true
        if r == rows - 1 or c == cols - 1: atlantic = true
        for each in-bounds neighbour not in seen with height <= heights[r][c]:   (water flows down)
            add it to seen, push it
    if pacific and atlantic: append [start_r, start_c] to result
return result
pacific_atlantic_water_flow.optimal:
climb(heights, sources):   (BFS uphill from one ocean's border cells)
    reached = grid of false; queue = empty deque
    for each (r, c) in sources: reached[r][c] = true, push (r, c)
    while the queue is not empty:
        (r, c) = pop from the front
        for each in-bounds neighbour (nr, nc) not reached with heights[nr][nc] >= heights[r][c]:
            reached[nr][nc] = true, push (nr, nc)   (reverse the flow: walk uphill from the sea)
    return reached
pacific_edge = left column + top row; atlantic_edge = right column + bottom row
from_pacific = climb(heights, pacific_edge), from_atlantic = climb(heights, atlantic_edge)
result = every [r, c] with from_pacific[r][c] and from_atlantic[r][c]
return result

clone_graph.brute:
if node is empty: return empty
originals = [], stack = [node]
while the stack is not empty:
    cur = pop the top; skip it if it is already in originals
    append cur to originals, push every neighbour of cur
copies = a fresh Node with the same value for each original
for each index i:
    for each neighbour nb of originals[i]:
        scan copies for the one whose value == nb.val   (linear search per edge)
        append it to copies[i].neighbors
return copies[0]
clone_graph.optimal:
if node is empty: return empty
clones = dict original -> copy, holding node -> new Node(node.val)
queue = deque of [node]
while the queue is not empty:
    cur = pop from the front
    for each neighbour nb of cur:
        if nb not in clones:   (first sight of nb: make its copy and plan to visit it)
            clones[nb] = new Node(nb.val)
            push nb to the back
        append clones[nb] to clones[cur].neighbors   (link copy to copy)
return clones[node]

number_of_connected_components.optimal:
find(parent, x): while parent[x] != x: parent[x] = parent[parent[x]], x = parent[x]; return x
parent[x] = x for every node, rank = all zeros, count = n   (every node is its own component)
for each edge (u, v):
    root_u = find(parent, u), root_v = find(parent, v)
    if root_u == root_v: continue   (already in the same component)
    if rank[root_u] < rank[root_v]: swap root_u and root_v
    parent[root_v] = root_u
    if rank[root_u] == rank[root_v]: rank[root_u] += 1
    count -= 1   (one merge = one component fewer)
return count

redundant_connection.brute:
neighbours = empty dict node -> neighbours among the edges accepted so far
for each edge (u, v) in order:
    seen = {u}, stack = [u]
    while the stack is not empty:   (is v already reachable from u?)
        cur = pop the top
        if cur == v: return [u, v]
        for each neighbour nb of cur not in seen: add nb to seen, push nb
    add v to neighbours[u] and u to neighbours[v]
return []
redundant_connection.optimal:
find(parent, x): while parent[x] != x: parent[x] = parent[parent[x]], x = parent[x]; return x
parent[x] = x for nodes 1..n, rank = all zeros   (union-find)
for each edge (u, v) in order:
    root_u = find(parent, u), root_v = find(parent, v)
    if root_u == root_v: return [u, v]   (u and v already connected: this edge closes the cycle)
    if rank[root_u] < rank[root_v]: swap root_u and root_v
    parent[root_v] = root_u
    if rank[root_u] == rank[root_v]: rank[root_u] += 1
return []

network_delay_time.brute:
dist = infinity for every node 1..n, dist[k] = 0
repeat n - 1 times:   (Bellman-Ford: every round relaxes every edge)
    for each edge (u, v, w) in times:
        if dist[u] + w < dist[v]:
            dist[v] = dist[u] + w
worst = max of dist over nodes 1..n
if worst is infinity: return -1
return worst

min_cost_to_connect_all_points.brute:
edges = every pair (i, j) as (manhattan distance, i, j), sorted   (Kruskal with a DFS cycle check)
neighbours = empty neighbour lists, total = 0
for each (w, u, v) in edges:
    seen = {u}, stack = [u]
    while the stack is not empty:   (DFS over the accepted edges: can u already reach v?)
        cur = pop the top
        for each neighbour nb of cur not in seen: add nb to seen, push nb
    if v not in seen:   (different trees: the edge is safe to take)
        add v to neighbours[u] and u to neighbours[v]
        total += w
return total

merge_intervals.brute:
result = copy of intervals
changed = true
while changed:
    changed = false
    for each pair i < j:
        a = result[i], b = result[j]
        if a.start <= b.end and b.start <= a.end:   (they overlap or touch)
            result[i] = [min of the starts, max of the ends]
            remove result[j]
            changed = true, restart the pair scan
return result sorted

meeting_rooms_ii.brute:
best = 0
for each meeting start:   (the peak always happens at some meeting's start)
    running = 0
    for each meeting (other_start, other_end):
        if other_start <= start and start < other_end: running += 1
    best = max(best, running)
return best
meeting_rooms_ii.optimal:
sort intervals by start
ends = empty min-heap of end times   (one entry per room in use right now)
rooms = 0
for each (start, end) in intervals:
    while ends is not empty and the smallest end <= start:
        pop the smallest end   (that meeting is over: its room is free again)
    push end   (this meeting takes a room)
    rooms = max(rooms, size of ends)
return rooms
